extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, podcast producers, and media industry executives
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for measuring podcast and digital audio audiences and for assessing the financial health and sustainability of digital news and podcast ventures. Includes guidance on metrics (downloads, listenership, device splits), measurement caveats, and revenue-model indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of download statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Download data are limited in that the statistics do not identify if the podcast downloaded was actually listened to, either in part or in its entirety, or how many different people may have listened to the podcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat raw download counts as synonymous with audience or consumption. Recognize downstream implications for advertisers and producers: downloads may overstate true listenership. Seek metrics that indicate actual listening (play starts, time listened, completion) rather than relying solely on file-request counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for standardized definition of 'download'
rubrics_metrics.description: A group comprised of staff from several public radio stations and networks released a report proposing new standards for defining a 'download' to identify and address ways that existing technologies could artificially inflate download statistics—such as bots or progressive downloading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt or align with industry definitions that exclude known inflation sources (bot traffic) and account for progressive download behaviors to improve comparability and reduce artificial inflation of counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt third-party audience measurement (Nielsen Digital Audio Ratings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nielsen announced it will begin to measure on-demand audio and podcasting as part of its Digital Audio Ratings Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established third‑party measurement services where possible to obtain comparable, industry-recognized metrics that advertisers and partners can trust. Integrate such ratings into audience reporting and sales materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use advanced metrics platforms and formats for granular listenership
rubrics_metrics.description: Panoply launched Megaphone, a content management system that can gather more granular data on listenership. The use of a format other than MP3s—such as that developed by Acast—is capable of delivering advanced metrics for advertisers, but it is a more expensive platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider investing in platform/tools (CMS, alternative delivery formats) that provide richer listen analytics (device-level, engagement, completion). Balance the benefits of granular data against additional costs and platform-dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure device preferences and segment by device
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile devices are increasingly preferred over desktops or laptops for podcast listening (e.g., 64% said they were listening 'most often' on a mobile device in 2016; Libsyn reported 69% of downloads requested from mobile in 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment audience metrics by device type (mobile vs desktop vs other) because consumption patterns and monetization opportunities differ by device. Use device breakdowns when planning distribution and ad strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple audience metrics and appropriate recall periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Different measures capture different aspects of audience: 21% of Americans age 12+ said they listened to a podcast in the past month, while 36% said they had ever listened to a podcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report a combination of metrics (past-month listeners, ever-listened, downloads, time-spent, share-of-audio-listening) to give a fuller picture of reach and engagement. Choose the recall period and metric that match the evaluation goal (reach vs penetration vs engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess podcast business models and revenue diversification
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising constitutes the dominant revenue stream for podcasts, but podcasters are experimenting with direct support (Patreon, Kickstarter), grants, subscriptions ('freemium'), and live events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating commercial sustainability, look beyond advertising revenue to the diversity of revenue streams and experimentation with alternative models. Track which models are generating earned income and consider combining multiple streams to reduce reliance on a single source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate financial health of local digital news publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Many local digital publishers report modest revenue: two-thirds generated $100,000 a year or less in 2014, about half generated $50,000 or less; 72% reported local advertising as making up half or more of total revenue; 81% of surveyed sites were for-profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete financial indicators—annual revenue bands, profitability, revenue composition (share from local advertising vs earned income), and organizational form (for-profit vs nonprofit)—to assess the viability and resilience of local digital publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit digital news revenue composition and sustainability indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Knight Foundation analysis of 20 nonprofit outlets, foundation funding accounted for 58% of total revenue in 2013, earned income about 23%, and individual donations/membership showed growth (average donors up 18%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprofit news outlets, track the share of foundation/grant funding vs earned income and individual donations, donor counts and median donation size, and year-over-year trends to assess sustainability and diversification progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for the small share of podcasts in total audio listening
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Edison Research Share of Ear, only 2% of all audio listening time is spent using podcasts, compared to 54% for AM/FM radio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place podcast audience metrics in the context of overall audio consumption: a growing audience may still represent a small share of total listening time. Use share-of-time metrics when comparing audio formats or making investment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize radio stations/formats when analyzing audience share
rubrics_metrics.description: Nielsen distinguishes 'all-news' and 'news/talk/information' stations; the all-news cohort garnered about 1% of overall audience share while news/talk/information held about 11% among ages 12+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze radio and audio audiences by program/format categories because audience share and trends vary substantially by format. Avoid aggregating dissimilar formats when drawing conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer audited and platform-verified metrics for circulation and traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Pew uses Alliance for Audited Media for circulation figures and comScore for digital traffic; analysts removed web entities whose traffic shifts were due to measurement changes rather than organic audience behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audited sources (Alliance for Audited Media, Nielsen, comScore) and verify that observed changes reflect actual behavior rather than measurement artifacts. When platform measurement methods change, adjust samples or note caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document sample selection and measurement caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Several cited studies rely on curated or nonprobability samples (e.g., McLellan/Tow-Knight survey, Knight Foundation sample) and Pew notes such samples 'do not purport to be exhaustive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting or interpreting findings, explicitly state sample type and limitations (curated list, nonprobability) and caution about generalizability. Where possible, triangulate with other data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize year-to-year revenue or audience changes with external events
rubrics_metrics.description: Univision's revenue dipped in 2015 after a 2014 windfall related to the FIFA World Cup; such events can produce one-off effects in year-over-year comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret trends with awareness of special events or cyclical factors that may inflate or depress a particular year's metrics. Annotate time series data to indicate known exogenous influences.
